findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with debris. The PIC was informed and cleaned/sanitized the ice machine during today’s visit. Ensure the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized frequently to avoid an accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The inspector observed the door and shelving of the walk-in cooler to have exposed wood. Ensure this bare wood is sealed prior to the next routine inspection. 

The inspector observed the ceiling tiles above the bathroom hand sink to be water damaged and soiled with mold. The PIC was informed that the tiles need to be replaced with non-absorbent tiles prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed walls and some shelving of the walk-in cooler to have bare wood. The paint on the door of the walk-in is damaged exposing bare wood, and the wood below the ventilation system in the walk-in appears to be untreated/uncoated. Ensure these wood surfaces are sealed to prevent moisture absorption and mold/bacterial accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the walk-in cooler fail to maintain proper cooling temperatures during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that the door to the walk-in was kept open during food preparation. While the cooler was able to recover and restore proper cold holding, fluctuations outside of the safe holding parameters should be avoided. Ensure that the PIC is monitoring cold holding temperatures and preventing improper cold holding in the facility. A follow-up will be conducted on August 11th to ensure the cooler is being properly monitored.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(I) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (I) EMPLOYEES are properly maintaining the temperatures of TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOODS during hot and cold holding through daily oversight of the EMPLOYEES’ routine monitoring of FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following food items to be above the maximum safe cold holding temperature in the walk-in cooler (all probed):
1. Chili (50.8F)
2. Two large containers of raw chicken (50.8F)
4. Taco meat (48.7F)

CORRECTED: Inspector waited at facility and confirmed that walk-in cooler reached safe cold-holding temperatures relatively quickly. PIC stated that the door of the cooler was open for an extended period during food prep. Ensure the door remains closed as much as possible to ensure proper cold holding. Discussed maintaining cooler temperature logs to aid in temperature monitoring.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed upright freezer in the dry storage area to have an accumulation of food debris and ice at the bottom of the freezer. Ensure freezers are cleaned frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil and debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled with dust/debris:
1. Above and around ventilation in the walk-in cooler
2. Baffles of the hood system

Ensure these areas are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed walls and some shelving of the walk-in cooler to have bare wood. The paint on the door of the walk-in is damaged exposing bare wood, and the wood below the ventilation system in the walk-in appears to be untreated/uncoated. Ensure these wood surfaces are sealed to prevent moisture absorption and mold/bacterial accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed mushrooms in the prep cooler to be stored in their original can after opening. PIC was informed that food must be transferred to a new container after opening. The can’s integrity is not maintained after opening, and thus poses a cross-contamination hazard for the contents of the can. The mushrooms were transferred to a new container during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Raw eggs were observed to be stored above mashed potatoes, and raw beef was observed to be stored directly atop cooked chili. PIC was informed of proper storage order practices. Storing raw ingredients above ready-to-eat ingredients can result in cross-contamination.  A follow-up will be conducted on Friday, April 25th to ensure compliance.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution prepared in the kitchen, although there was cooking taking place in the kitchen. Although there were no customers present and no dishes being prepared, ensure there is a sanitizer solution available at all times during food preparation, cooking, or service. A follow-up will be conducted on April 25th to ensure compliance.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed chili in the walk-in cooler to bear a date exceeding 7 days (marked 4/6). The chili was actively in use in a warmer for service. Sliced tomatoes stored in the prep cooler were also exceeding the 7 days mark on their label (marked 4/15). PIC was informed of improper date marking, and the items were discarded. Date marking practices will be spot checked during the follow-up scheduled for April 25th.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed cut tomatoes and cut lettuce in the prep cooler bottom to be missing appropriate date marks. Cut tomato and cut lettuce are considered time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. TCS foods must be marked with a date mark if stored longer than 24 hours after preparation and discarded after 7 days. A follow-up will be conducted on May 2nd to ensure compliance.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed bags of raw chicken thawing in the triple sink. The faucet was on over the thawing chicken, but the drip was inadequate to agitate and float off loose particles. PIC was informed that thawing methods were inadequate, and the water pressure was increased from the faucet. Ensure proper thawing methods are utilized to prevent the accumulation of bacteria in the chicken, resulting in food-borne illness. Thawing methods will be spot checked during the follow-up conducted on April 25th.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed onions stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Also observed cut tomatoes and sauce stored in the prep cooler to have no protective covering. Ensure food items are protected from splash, dust, or other contamination during storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed upright freezer in the dry storage area to have an accumulation of food debris and ice at the bottom of the freezer. Ensure freezers are cleaned frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil and debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed window and fan behind hood system to be soiled with grease and dust deposits. The walls above the prep cooler were also observed to be soiled with dust and debris. Ensure the walls, windows, and floors are cleaned frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed personal food items stored along with food items for the consumer. PIC was informed that personal food items pose a cross-contamination hazard when stored with food for the facility. Ensure a designated area is used (ex. Plastic bin or bottom shelf) to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed no hand washing soap available for use at bar hand washing sink. Soap was provided during inspection. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed roll of paper towels in basin of bar hand washing sink. Paper towels were removed during inspection. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: Observed no sanitizing solution available for use in kitchen during food preparation. Sanitizing solution was made during inspection and tested at 200 ppm Cl-. 

 (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed no hand washing soap available for use at bar hand washing sink. Soap was provided during inspection. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed gap to outdoors under screen door to kitchen. Main door was closed during inspection. Fill gap or keep main door closed at all times.

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: Observed no sanitizing solution available for use in kitchen during food preparation. Sanitizing solution was made during inspection and tested at 200 ppm Cl-. 

 (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: Observed wet mop head to be stored head down in mop bucket.

  After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed paint on interior and exterior door of walk-in-cooler door to be peeling. Repaint interior and exterior of walk-in-cooler door so that it is smooth and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
